title: Image Grading: eccentricity max can be set to 1.00, which is a threshold the pipeline can never exceed - the check becomes inert with no warning
summary: Already closed by an earlier fix wave; verified by inspection AND by reverting the production constant. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/image_grading_settings.dart now clamps every threshold to what the detector can actually report: _eccentricityMaxInput = 0.94 (one step below skotiq_imaging::DETECTION_MAX_ECCENTRICITY = 0.95, confirmed at native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/stats.rs:166 - grading rejects on `ecc > threshold`, so a threshold AT the ceiling is as dead as one above it), _hfrFloorPx = 1.0 (StarDetectionConfig.min_hfr, below which every frame with stars is a reject) and _hfrCeilingPx = 20.0 (hfr_radius, above which the gate never fires). The old 0.0-1.0 and 0.1-50 ranges are gone. Values persisted before the bounds existed still load unclamped, so _hfrInertNote / _eccentricityInertNote append a plain-language warning to the row subtitle. NOT FIXED, deliberately: the finding's star-count clause ('min max 100000 rejects every frame on any realistic sensor'). Unlike min_hfr and DETECTION_MAX_ECCENTRICITY there is no pipeline bound on detected star count - min_area = 9 px means a large sensor on a dense field can genuinely report tens of thousands - so any cap would be an arbitrary capability removal, and the failure mode is loud anyway (every frame lands in the reject folder) rather than the silent never-fires case the finding is about.
revert_check: Set image_grading_settings.dart:47 back to `const double _eccentricityMaxInput = 1.0;` -> 'eccentricity clamps to a value the detector can exceed' FAILED (9 passed, 1 failed). Restored -> 10/10 pass.
caveats: The fix is uncommitted working-tree work from an earlier wave (git diff HEAD shows +71/-7 on that file). Reported as already-correct rather than not-real: the finding WAS real when it was filed.

title: Sequence checkpoints and logs are written to the platform app-support directory, ignoring the configured data directory
summary: Partly closed already, two roots still open; I fixed both. ALREADY CLOSED by an earlier wave: the GUI checkpoint directory. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:82 resolveGuiCheckpointDirectory() now anchors it on the parent of the OPEN DATABASE (resolveDefaultDatabaseFile honours SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR), so the phantom 'Recover Sequence?' modal offering another instance's run is structurally impossible, and adoptLegacyGuiCheckpoint carries a pre-upgrade checkpoint forward only when the override is unset. STILL OPEN, now fixed: (1) LoggingService resolved its log root straight from getApplicationSupportDirectory(). That folder is per-application, not per-instance, so a headless daemon started beside the GUI with its own SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR still opened the GUI's rolling skotiq.log and pointed the native appender at it - which is exactly the 'Log directory: /home/.../com.skotiq.desktop/logs' line the audit reproduced while SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR pointed elsewhere. (2) resolveHostCheckpointDirectory() in the headless host did the same, so two daemons each given their own data directory shared one skotiq_session.checkpoint. Added packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/utils/skotiq_data_directory.dart - skotiqDataDirEnv + resolveSkotiqDataDirectory(), one rule matching what Rust already applies to SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR (bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:5190) and what apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/handlers/calibration_handlers.dart:110 already open-coded - and routed both roots through it. LoggingService gained an injectable `environment` seam; resolveHostCheckpointDirectory gained `environment` + `applicationSupportDirectoryProvider` seams. Behaviour is byte-identical when SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR is unset. A concurrent agent independently fixed the third root (apps/desktop/lib/desktop_logging_init.dart, prepareDesktopLogDirectory/resolveDesktopDataRoot + test/headless/desktop_log_directory_test.dart); I left that file alone rather than clobber their in-flight edit.
revert_check: LOGGING: replaced the whole call site at logging_service.dart:190-199 - `final appDir = await resolveSkotiqDataDirectory(environment: _environment, applicationSupportDirectoryProvider: _applicationSupportDirectoryProvider);` - with the pre-fix `final appDir = await _applicationSupportDirectoryProvider();` -> 'SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR moves logging off the shared application-support folder' FAILED ('Differ at offset 8'). Restored -> 3/3 pass. CHECKPOINT: replaced host_checkpoint_directory.dart:24-27 with the pre-fix `final dataRoot = await (applicationSupportDirectoryProvider ?? getApplicationSupportDirectory)();` (and the import back to path_provider) -> 2 of 3 FAILED ('an instance data directory owns its own checkpoint folder' emitted /tmp/ns-shared-support*/checkpoints; 'a relative override still fails loudly' did not throw). Restored -> 3/3 pass.
caveats: Full suites run per the shared-file rule. apps/desktop: 980 pass / 5 fail, every failure a `loading ... [E]` compile error from a concurrent agent's in-flight edit to packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/node_duration_provider.dart (SequenceTimeEstimator / sequencerOverheadConfigProvider undefined) - nothing to do with this change. skotiq_core: 5343 pass / 17 fail / 4 skip, and a second run 20 minutes later produced a different failure set (9), which is the same concurrent churn (weather_safety_nothing_to_safe, nina_sequence_fidelity, transient_alert_service load failure). Attribution argument: SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR is not set in this environment, so resolveSkotiqDataDirectory falls straight through to the existing provider and the change is a strict no-op for every test that does not pass `environment:` explicitly. All four logging suites (logging_service, logging_service_stream, logging_export_retention, logging_data_directory) pass 21/21. dart analyze clean on all six files; dart format clean.
